text:
Situation: Potassium chloride has been on FDA's shortage list since 2019-06-10 with a status of To Be Discontinued. As of 2026-10-21 the shortage has persisted for 88 months. Current inventory across Corvale sites shows potassium chloride injection products ranging from 2.7 to 19.6 days on hand, with the 29.8G/1000ML 50ML bag at Corvale East critically low at 2.7 days.

Why (FDA record): FDA posted the potassium chloride shortage on 2019-06-10. An OAI inspection at Baxter Healthcare Corporation (FEI 2618677) ended on 2016-10-03, 980 days before the shortage posting. Additional OAI inspections at that plant occurred on 2010-08-26, 2013-04-19, 2014-02-11, and 2015-05-01, with warning letters issued on 2011-01-20 and 2013-05-31. A later OAI inspection at Baxter Healthcare Corporation (FEI 1416980) ended on 2024-08-01 and another on 2026-04-02, with a warning letter issued on 2026-09-29. Pfizer Healthcare India Private Limited (FEI 3008316085) received an OAI classification on 2019-09-06, 88 days after the shortage posting, and a warning letter on 2020-03-25.

Our position: The rule-selected alternate manufacturer is A-S Medication Solutions, which is not on FDA's shortage list today and its label names no plant we could place. Four additional manufacturers (Advagen Pharma Limited, Affordable Pharmaceuticals LLC, Ajenat Pharmaceuticals LLC, American Health Packaging) are also not on FDA's shortage list but similarly lack identifiable plant information on their labels. Multiple potassium chloride injection presentations are below 10 days supply at Corvale East.

Recommended actions:
1. Buyer to initiate qualification and purchase from A-S Medication Solutions for potassium chloride injection presentations; requires P&T committee approval for formulary addition.
2. Buyer to evaluate Advagen Pharma Limited, Affordable Pharmaceuticals LLC, Ajenat Pharmaceuticals LLC, and American Health Packaging as secondary sources; each requires P&T committee approval for formulary addition.
3. Buyer to request plant identification information from all five manufacturers' labels; requires Quality Assurance approval for supplier qualification.
4. Pharmacy director to allocate existing potassium chloride injection stock to highest-acuity areas; requires medical director approval for allocation protocol.

Not recommended: Switching patients to alternative potassium salts or changing dosing regimens; clinical changes are for the treating clinicians and the committee.
